newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares lose their shine by close, CHH ends down.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares lose their shine by close, CHH ends down.

text.p: * NZ shares lose intraday gains but end in positive
* Carter end lower after result and earlier gains
* Telecom result seen dictating direction
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +2.96 at 2,303.16
320 -3 * NZSC cap index +4.09 at 5,025.83
330 +6 * NZMC cap index -3.04 at 1,869.76
347 +2 * Volume NZ$61.3 million. Futures untraded
668 -2 * Other movers - +15
The New Zealand share market closed in positive territory on Tuesday, helped by lower interest rates and another big rise on Wall Street.
But the top 40 index ended just 2.96 up at 2303.16 after being up 15 points earlier in the session.
After rising sharply on Monday following a Reserve Bank call for tighter monetary conditions, interest rates eased back, helping the equities market.
"People think the Reserve Bank has been overly cautious," said Merrill Lynch broker Tim Koller. "Today's performance shows there's good demand underpinning this market."
Highlight of the day was the annual result of Carter Holt Harvey, which reported a profit on expectations at NZ$251 million.
The forester's stock rose six cents after the result as investors approved progress on the cost cutting front and noises from the company that the pulp price recession had bottomed.
But the stock dived at the close after a big buyer pulled back from the market. It ended three cents down at $3.20.
However, fellow paper maker Fletcher Paper held its gains, ending six ahead at $3.30.

The market's direction is likely to be set by heavyweight Telecom, which reports its annual result at midday on Wednesday. Analysts forecast a flat net profit of NZ$718 million before provisions. Substantial provisions are forecast.
Telecom closed two cents down at $6.68.
Sky City closed up 15 cents at $6.65 on good turnover. Brokers said the stock was playing catch-up with the market after languishing during the recent market rally.
